A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AdaLRS work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and Appendices A-C are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM and VLM pretraining experiments, benchmark results, learning-rate trajectories, a backtracking ablation and continual-pretraining experiments.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds downstream LLM generation evaluations and experiments varying AdaLRS hyperparameters.

M1.justification: Appendix A revises inconclusive trials to restore model states and reset history/threshold, and moves threshold tightening to the ordinary LR-maintenance branch. Section 2.1 broadens scaling factors from coprime integers to multiplicatively independent reals; Equation 1 corrects the failed-upscaling test. These are limited revisions to the retained loss-slope search and backtracking procedure.

E1.justification: Section 3.1 adds instruction tuning on Infinity-Instruct and evaluation on Alpaca-Gen and KNIGHT-Gen, extending LLM coverage from pretraining loss/perplexity to downstream open-ended generation. Existing pretraining data and VLM benchmarks remain. DetailCaps-4870 already appeared in v1 Table 3 and is not new coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain baselines with AdaLRS disabled under cosine or WSD scheduling. The downstream evaluations use the same comparator models, and Table 4 compares AdaLRS parameter variants with an AdaLRS-disabled baseline. No additional competing learning-rate search method is evaluated.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a downstream LLM evaluation pipeline involving SFT on 6M Infinity-Instruct samples before generation testing. It also introduces controlled variations of scaling and decay factors in Table 4. These expand the evaluation design; the original Table 1 pretraining recipes and WSD procedure remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Section 3.4 and Table 4 investigate sensitivity to upscaling, downscaling and decay factors under both small and large initial learning rates. This adds a substantive test of dependence on AdaLRS's own hyperparameters. The existing scheduler, backtracking and continual-pretraining analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical repeated-run counts, seed summaries, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The added results retain the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds Alpaca-Gen and KNIGHT-Gen scores while retaining its original loss/PPL values; Table 4 adds sensitivity results. Table 3 changes DetailCaps-4870 scores and averages and exchanges MMVet/MMStar entries in the Large/Small LR rows. For example, Large-LR MMVet changes from 44.47/44.33 to 31.47/30.50 for AdaLRS/baseline. These are revised reported results, not established performance gains between versions.

T1.justification: Section 2.2.1 adds an SGD/Taylor-expansion argument using a gradient Lipschitz constant and deriving an optimal step size of 1/C_Lip to support the central shared-optimum hypothesis. Appendix B generalizes Theorem B.1 and its irrationality argument from coprime integers to multiplicatively independent reals. The existing convergence and geometric-decay proofs are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract explicitly extends the robustness claim to varying AdaLRS hyperparameter settings. The central claims about single-run learning-rate search, shared optima, convergence and improved pretraining performance remain substantially unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 3.4 adds a mechanism explanation for similar final learning rates under different decay settings: overshooting triggers downscaling in one case, while stronger decay prevents that adjustment in another. Appendix C retains the previous limitations concerning excessive initial learning rates, fine-grained convergence and grid-search estimates of the optimum.

D1.justification: v3 specifies the new LLM SFT dataset and 6M-sample count and lists the coefficient combinations used in Table 4, including noninteger scaling factors and multiple decay factors. Existing hardware, training-cost and implementation disclosures remain; no new code-access information is provided.

R1.justification: Three references are added for the DetailCaps benchmark, Infinity-Instruct and the work cited for the generation evaluations, appearing as references 17, 27 and 47 in v3. The related-work discussion and positioning against scaling laws, hyperparameter transfer, automated search and Hypergradient Descent remain substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, evaluation description, conclusion and author/header text receive localized edits. A hyperparameter-robustness subsection is inserted before the retained ablation and continual-pretraining subsections. The overall organization and most existing prose remain.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 4, expands Table 2 with two benchmark rows and moves the DetailCaps-4870 column within Table 3. Figures and surrounding text are repositioned through page reflow, but all four existing figures retain their plotted content and overall design.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the downstream generation tests examine whether LLM pretraining benefits translate to practical outputs, and Table 4 tests dependence on previously fixed AdaLRS coefficients. These provide useful additional validation. The gain is limited: the new one-step SGD argument does not establish the broad training-loss convexity claim, Table 3's numerical revisions are unexplained, and Algorithm 1 retains a coprimality condition inconsistent with the generalized real-valued factors.
